findings.section: Core / Question 5 (rds-q005), Why
findings.quote: Through the proxy, [most connections stay alive during failovers](../facts/rds-proxy.md#rds-proxy-failover-idle-connections-kept).
findings.type: claims: link to a fact that is not verified (disputed); technical: condition dropped
findings.evidence: facts show rds-proxy-failover-idle-connections-kept: status disputed, rev 3 entail vote partial ('The quote limits the behavior to applications that maintain their own connection pool; the claim drops that condition'). Source docs/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.howitworks: "For applications that maintain their own connection pool, going through RDS Proxy means that most connections stay alive during failovers or other disruptions. Only connections that are in the middle of a transaction or SQL statement are canceled." findings.section: Signals and traps; Traps; Choose it or not (Amazon RDS or RDS Custom or a database on Amazon EC2); also 2-deep.md 'Amazon RDS runs the database engine while you keep the queries' step 4 and card rds-c032

Add 'for Oracle or SQL Server' wherever RDS Custom is the answer (needs a fact for the engine list).
findings.resolution: fix-26 (softened, no ungrounded engine claim added): no verified fact states the RDS Custom engine list (the scope qualifier is not a display), so the book does not state it. 2-deep.md step 4 now says 'Check that RDS Custom runs your engine; if not, use Amazon EC2.'; 1-fast.md signal row 'access to the operating system' now has the guard 'RDS Custom does not run your engine: Amazon EC2', and the trap rds-trap-rds-gives-os-access adds 'If RDS Custom does not run your engine, use Amazon EC2.' findings.section: Encryption at rest is chosen at creation and covers every copy, step 4
findings.quote: Clients use [Transport Layer Security (TLS)](../facts/rds.md#rds-tls-all-engines). To require it, you change a parameter. A default parameter group stays as it is, so [create a new parameter group.](../facts/rds.md#rds-parameter-group-default-not-modifiable)
findings.type: technical: oversimplified, outdated for the chapter's engine
findings.evidence: Fact rds-tls-force-postgresql (verified): "The `rds.force_ssl` parameter default value is 1 (on) for RDS for PostgreSQL version 15 and later. For all other RDS for PostgreSQL major versions 14 and older, the default value of this parameter is 0 (off)." For RDS for PostgreSQL 15 and later (the default version today), TLS is already required with the default parameter group; a parameter change is needed only for older versions or other engines. Say so, with the fact link.
findings.resolution: fix-26: 2-deep.md encryption step 4 now reads 'On RDS for PostgreSQL, `rds.force_ssl` requires it, and it is on by default from [version 15 and later](rds-tls-force-postgresql). A default parameter group stays as it is, so [create a new parameter group.]'

findings.section: Force TLS in a custom parameter group, steps 2, 4 and 5
findings.quote: "expect": "One row: the default value, the apply type (static or dynamic), and True ... For PostgreSQL 15 and later, the default value is 1."
findings.type: technical: task teaches a no-op; break step may not show the lesson
findings.evidence: Fact rds-tls-force-postgresql: default 1 for version 15 and later. Step 1 takes the family of the default PostgreSQL version (expect: 'for example postgres17'), so step 5 sets rds.force_ssl to the value it already has, and the task title 'Force TLS in a custom parameter group' changes nothing for the reader's default engine. Step 4 also accepts a 'group was not found' error as 'the lesson is the same', but a not-found error does not show that a default group cannot be modified (rds-parameter-group-default-not-modifiable). Fix: say in the text that the custom group is needed to change any parameter (for example on PostgreSQL 14 or MySQL require_secure_transport, with a fact), and drop the not-found clause or tell the reader that the break step then proves nothing.
findings.resolution: fix-26: rds-t03 replaced with the same commands (the CLI report hash stays valid). Title is now 'Change a parameter in a custom parameter group'. Step 2 expect: on 15 and later the default is already 1; on 14 and older it is 0 and this task is how you turn it on. Step 4 expect: a not-found error means the step proves nothing. Step 4 explain: 'To change any parameter, you create a custom DB parameter group'. Step 5 expect: on 15 and later the value was already 1, the group now holds it as your own setting. The 2-deep Try it callout now says 'Change a parameter: a default group refuses, and a custom group accepts.'

findings.section: Storage autoscaling grows storage before it fills but never shrinks it, heading and step 2
findings.quote: **RDS watches free space.** RDS scales when free space is at or below [10 percent of the allocated storage](../facts/rds.md#rds-storage-autoscaling-trigger-free-space) for [at least five minutes](../facts/rds.md#rds-storage-autoscaling-trigger-five-minutes).
findings.type: technical: condition dropped; heading overclaims
findings.evidence: Fact rds-storage-autoscaling-trigger-five-minutes scope: "one of three trigger conditions"; rds-storage-autoscaling-trigger-free-space scope: "the previous modification must have finished optimizing". full:amazonrds-userguide line 17547 [Limitations of storage autoscaling]: "Autoscaling can't completely prevent storage-full situations for large data loads. This is because further storage modifications can't be made until storage optimization completes on the instance". The step reads as the full trigger and the heading says storage grows 'before it fills'; add the third condition and the large-data-load limit.
findings.resolution: fix-26: step 2 now reads 'It scales when free space falls to [10 percent of the allocated storage] for [at least five minutes], after the last change finishes optimizing.' The large-load limit is in 1-fast.md as the guard of the 'unpredictable storage growth' signal ('a large one-time data load: allocate the storage first'); it could not be linked in 2-deep.md because the only display of rds-storage-autoscaling-large-loads has a contraction (L803), see fact request fr-0088. The heading text is fixed by brief.json (R4) and was not changed.

findings.section: A read replica receives changes later and serves only reads
findings.quote: Why can a replica show old data? Changes arrive after the commit, so its data [might be stale](../facts/rds.md#rds-read-replica-use-source-unavailable).
findings.type: claims: link does not support the sentence (scope differs)
findings.evidence: Fact rds-read-replica-use-source-unavailable quote: "For this use case, keep in mind that the data on the read replica might be stale because the source DB instance is unavailable." The fact is about reads while the source is unavailable; the sentence uses it for general asynchronous lag. Link a lag fact instead (for example rds-faq-multi-az-for-write-availability, whose claim covers lag that 'can vary significantly', or rds-replica-size-as-much-as-source 'replication lag is likely to increase').
findings.resolution: fix-26: the sentence now reads 'Why can a replica show old data? With [asynchronous replication](rds-compare-replication-sync-async), changes arrive after the commit.' The two suggested lag facts could not be used: their displays hold `lag`, a banned term variant (L901).

findings.section: Extended / Question 18, answer and Why
findings.quote: Use Amazon RDS for MySQL, create a read replica, and set the read_only parameter of the replica to 0. ... After this parameter change on the replica, the team adds its indexes and tables there, and changes from the source keep arriving.
findings.type: claims: mechanism without a fact; technical: oversimplified, against an AWS recommendation
findings.evidence: No verified fact names the read_only parameter (rds-replica-mysql-logical-writable only says 'You can enable the MariaDB or MySQL read replica to be writable'). full:amazonrds-userguide line 16252 [Monitoring replication lag] lists as a common cause of lag: "Writing to tables with indexes on a read replica. If the `read_only` parameter is not set to 0 on the read replica, it can break replication." Line 26188 [Recommendations]: "Your DB instance has a read replica in writable mode, which allows updates from clients. We recommend that you set the `read_only` parameter to `TrueIfReplica` so that the read replicas isn't in writable mode." So 'changes from the source keep arriving' hides the lag and breakage risk, and the chapter heading says a replica 'serves only reads'. Ground read_only=0 in a fact (line 16159 'set the read_only parameter to 0 in the DB parameter group for the read replica') and name the risk, or replace the question.
findings.resolution: fix-26: the premise is wrong. Verified fact rds-faq-read-replica-mysql-ddl is in the question's facts and the key's why links it; its claim names the parameter ('by setting the read_only parameter to 0') and its display is 'setting the “read_only” parameter to “0.”'. The AWS FAQ describes this use (DDL on a MySQL replica). The lag risk is real but does not change the key, and an explanation edit would reset a verified question (R5). The chapter now teaches the writable MySQL or MariaDB replica in a Go deeper block of the read replica subsection, which also addresses the heading tension.
